outcomes: Decides whether a worse position can be held by a fortress
Spots an enemy fortress he cannot break and says what would break it
Does not assume that more material always wins
sources: items IBds62-18..22 in content/items/lesson-ds62.json (tablebase claims checked by tools/validate.py)
shipped puzzle items IL-P6kZn, IL-Eoi1d, IL-dNitq (Lichess puzzles, CC0, tablebase claims)

steps.text: In **Ahead in material, still unable to win** you built a fortress from a given imbalance. Now judge any position. Behind in material, ask: can I set up something he cannot break? Ahead, ask: can he? Three questions: is there an entry square or a breakthrough? Does the weaker side always have a safe waiting move? Can the stronger side force a zugzwang?

**Rule of thumb:** more material does not always win. A fortress holds when the stronger side has no entry square and no breakthrough, and the defender always has a safe waiting move. In the next three positions the black pawn is one step from queening, and where the draw holds it rests on stalemate: the queen leaves Black no legal move. Change the pawn's file, or move a piece, and see which change matters. The tablebase gives the verdicts.

steps.title: Queen against a pawn: what breaks it?
steps.prompt: White is to move with a queen against a pawn. Predict whether White can win, then check. Look at what differs from the first position.

steps.text: No labels now. Some positions hold, some are broken by a small change, and some need exact moves. Ask the three questions, then predict. The next four exercises are silent.

steps.prompt: In a lost-looking position of yours, what would you check first to see whether a fortress exists: an entry square, a breakthrough or a waiting move? Write your answer down.
